To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DNA fragmentation was revealed in 20h after irradiation of human lymphocytes by UV light at doses of 150 J/m2 and higher.
the DNA damage in the human lymphocyte nuclei, induced by UV light, leads to the development of apoptosis, which is accompanied by the release of cytochrome c into the cytoplasm.
DNA damage is a key event in the induction of apoptosis in human lymphocytes after UV irradiation, which is mediated by p53 protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of UV light-induced apoptosis development in human peripheral lymphocytes.
the study of apoptosis development in the lymphocytes of human blood after UV irradiation.
the study of the mechanism of apoptosis in human lymphocytes induced by UV irradiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the p53-dependent and the receptor caspase pathway are the main pathways of apoptosis development in UV-irradiated human lymphocytes, and the p53-independent and the mitochondrial pathway play the secondary role.
the p53 protein is a key factor for apoptosis development in lymphocytes, induced after UV-irradiations.
UV radiation induces the formation of single strand breaks and double strand breaks in the DNA of human lymphocytes and this leads to the activation of caspase cascade and apoptosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
apoptosis in human lymphocytes induced by UV light occurs in the presence of cytochrome c in mitochondria.

apoptosis in human lymphocytes induced by UV irradiation occurs via the p53-dependent and the receptor caspase-dependent pathways, which can be distinguished by the dynamics of DNA damage and the content of cytochrome c in cytoplasm.
apoptosis development is a result of DNA damage and p53 activation, which leads to the activation of receptor caspases and cytochrome C release.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the level of DNA damage in the cells of the lymphoid organs is a key factor in the development of apoptosis, and the intensity of this process in human lymphoid organs is determined by the level of cytochrome c in mitochondria.
the level of DNA damage in human lymphocytes is directly related to the level of cytochrome c release into cytoplasm.
the UV-induced DNA damage is a necessary, but not sufficient condition for apoptosis development.
